you should supply a buffer name and then use @values to assign the buffers for each instance
double-click to look at the buffer contents
mcp.record~ ted 1 @chans 4 @values ted alice carol bob
start and stop recording all instances and trigger a sound
mc.play~ ted 1 @chans 4 @loop 1 @values ted alice carol bob

The mcp.record~ object combines multiple instances of record~ in the MC wrapper. Each record~ instance can record into a different buffer~ object. Use the @values feature of the MC Wrapper to assign the buffers you want to use.
must specify a buffer name and a number of channels to get multichannel behavior

The mc.record~ object has a multichannel inlet rather than separate inlets. You need to specify a number of channels as a second argument to mc.record~, then each input channel will write to the corresponding channel of the associated buffer~ object.
